name: Aga Khan Foundation International Scholarship Programme (ISP)
host: Aga Khan Foundation (AKDN); applications through the AKF / Aga Khan Education Board office in Pakistan
coverage: Tuition and living costs, awarded as 50% grant and 50% loan (the loan part is repaid with a service charge)
amount: Need-based; the amount is set per student. The 50% loan is repayable after studies
level: Master's (priority); PhD considered (first two years only)
fields: Any field; no preferred fields are listed on the official page. CS/AI is acceptable
eligibility: Nationals of listed developing countries (Pakistan is listed). Excellent academic record, admission to a reputable master's programme, and demonstrated financial need. Preference for young professionals under 30
english: No AKF test rule; it follows the host university's English requirement. An MOI letter works only if the university accepts it
gre: Not required (unless the university requires it)
deadline: The 2026-27 cycle is closed. The next cycle opens in early 2027; the international deadline is usually about 31 March, and the Pakistan office may set an earlier one
bond: None found (the loan half must be repaid)
fitReason: Pakistan is eligible and the award suits a Germany plan: German tuition is near-zero, so a grant plus soft loan could cover the blocked account and living costs. Need-based, so the applicant's modest budget helps. Apply in early 2027 for a Fall 2027 start.
steps: From January 2027, use the eligibility tool on the AKDN ISP page to get the Pakistan contact
Ask the AKF Pakistan / Aga Khan Education Board (Karachi) office for the 2027-28 form and the local deadline
Apply to German/EU universities in parallel (most German winter-semester deadlines are 15 Jan to 31 May)
Submit the form with transcripts, references, a budget and proof of financial need before the local deadline (expect about March)
Interview with the national committee; decisions come in June or July

name: Aga Khan Education Services / Education Board, Pakistan (local higher-education assistance)
host: AKES,P / Aga Khan Education Board for Pakistan
coverage: Mainly the local route into the AKF ISP; other local loans and grants are mostly for the Ismaili community
eligibility: Community-based schemes are mainly for Ismaili applicants; the ISP channel is open to all
deadline: Same as the AKF ISP (about March 2027, local date to be confirmed)
fitReason: Treat this as the office you apply to for the AKF ISP, not a separate award. Separate AKES schemes are probably community-restricted.
steps: Contact the Aga Khan Education Board Karachi office and ask for the ISP application route and any open schemes

name: Rotary Foundation Global Grant Scholarship
host: The Rotary Foundation, through a sponsoring Rotary club or district (Karachi clubs, District 3271 Sindh/Balochistan)
coverage: Tuition, living costs, travel and supplies, as budgeted by the sponsor club
amount: Minimum budget of US$30,000 per global grant (1 to 4 years)
fields: Must fit one of 7 areas of focus: peace, disease prevention and treatment, water and sanitation, maternal and child health, basic education, community economic development, environment. CS/AI qualifies only if framed around one of these (for example medical AI for eye disease, which matches the applicant's retinal-imaging project)
eligibility: Not a Rotarian or a relative or employee of one (some districts). Admission to the programme is needed before the grant is approved. Needs a sponsoring club in the home district and a host club near the university
english: Per university; Rotary sets no test
deadline: Rolling, but districts set internal deadlines, often 9 to 12 months ahead. The grant application must reach the Foundation at least 3 months before departure. For Fall 2027, approach clubs now (Oct-Dec 2026)
bond: None found; scholars are expected to stay engaged with Rotary
fitReason: Can be a large top-up (US$30k+) for Germany. The applicant's retinal-imaging deep-learning work maps onto 'disease prevention and treatment'. Success depends on persuading a Karachi club and a host club in Germany to co-sponsor.
steps: Use Rotary Club Locator to find Karachi clubs in District 3271 and ask about global grant scholarship sponsorship
Prepare a one-page pitch linking an AI master's to an area of focus (for example AI screening for diabetic retinopathy)
Get admission to the target programme
Club and district find a host club near the university; the club submits the global grant application in Rotary's Grant Center
Submit at least 3 months before departure, and follow the district's earlier internal deadline

name: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP)
coverage: Tuition, monthly living stipend, round-trip airfare, health insurance
fields: Development-related master's in about 44 participating programmes (economics, public policy, energy, environment, health, etc.). Pure CS/AI programmes are not participating programmes
eligibility: Developing-country national (Pakistan qualifies), no dual citizenship with a developed country. At least 3 years of paid full-time development-related work after the bachelor's, within the last 6 years, and currently employed. Unconditional admission to a participating programme
deadline: 2026 windows: 15 Jan-27 Feb and 30 Mar-29 May 2026. The 2027 call will likely use similar windows
bond: Expected to return home to contribute to development (moral commitment, weighted 30% in selection)
fitReason: Not eligible: the applicant has about 2 years of private-sector AI work, not 3+ years of development work, and CS/AI programmes are not on the participating list.
steps: Not recommended. Reconsider only after 3+ years of development-sector work and with a policy-oriented programme

name: Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) Scholarship Programme
coverage: Tuition, monthly stipend, medical insurance, travel
level: M.Sc. track only for Least Developed Member Countries; Merit Scholarship (MSP) is PhD/postdoc only
eligibility: M.Sc. track: citizens of about 20 Least Developed Member Countries, under 30, nominated by an institution. Pakistan is a member country but not an LDMC
deadline: Last cycle (2026-27) closed about 31 January 2026
fitReason: Not eligible for a master's: the M.Sc. track is limited to LDMCs, which do not include Pakistan. The Merit (MSP) track open to Pakistanis is PhD-level.
steps: No action for a master's. Note the MSP if a PhD is planned later

name: OPEC Fund (OFID) Scholarship Award
coverage: Formerly: tuition, living allowance, housing, insurance, travel (up to US$50,000)
eligibility: Developing-country nationals, under 32
deadline: Programme is being restructured and is not accepting applications (per directories, July 2026)
fitReason: Suspended, and CS/AI was never a priority field.
steps: Check opecfund.org in early 2027 for a relaunch

name: Gates Cambridge Scholarship
host: Gates Cambridge Trust, University of Cambridge
coverage: Full Cambridge fees, maintenance stipend, airfare, visa and immigration health surcharge
fields: Any Cambridge postgraduate course, e.g. MPhil in Advanced Computer Science / Machine Learning and Machine Intelligence
eligibility: Non-UK citizen applying to a full-time Cambridge graduate course. Outstanding academics (a 3.41 CGPA is weak for this), leadership and a commitment to improving others' lives
english: Cambridge requires IELTS/TOEFL or equivalent; an MOI letter is generally NOT accepted for Pakistani applicants
deadline: 2027 entry: the scholarship deadline is the course deadline, early December 2026 or early January 2027 for most international applicants
fitReason: Extremely competitive, and a 3.41 CGPA plus no IELTS make success unlikely. Apply only if already applying to Cambridge.
steps: Apply to a Cambridge MPhil via the Graduate Admissions portal by the course's funding deadline (Dec 2026/Jan 2027)
Tick the Gates Cambridge box and complete the Gates statement in the same form

name: Rhodes Scholarship (Pakistan constituency)
coverage: Oxford fees, stipend, airfare, visa/IHS
fields: Any Oxford course incl. MSc Advanced Computer Science
eligibility: Pakistani passport. For 2027 entry: aged 18-23 on 1 Oct 2026, or under 27 if the first degree was completed on/after 1 Oct 2025. The 2028 cycle shifts by a year. 2 awards for Pakistan
english: Oxford English requirement (test usually needed; MOI not generally accepted)
deadline: 2027 cycle ran 1 Jun-5 Aug 2026 (closed). The 2028 cycle is expected Jun-Aug 2027
fitReason: The age/graduation rules are tight and only 2 awards are given. A 3.41 CGPA is uncompetitive, and Fall 2027 has already been missed.
steps: Check the age rule on the Rhodes House Pakistan eligibility page
If eligible, apply Jun-Aug 2027 for 2028 entry

name: Bhutto STEM Scholarships at Oxford (Government of Sindh, Lady Margaret Hall / Oxford Pakistan Programme)
host: Sindh College Education Department + Oxford Pakistan Programme + Lady Margaret Hall
coverage: Tuition and living expenses at Oxford
amount: Full funding; 6 awards in 2026-27 (3 for women, 3 open merit)
level: Master's / MPhil / DPhil (STEM preferred, some preference for doctoral)
eligibility: Sindh CNIC, domicile and PRC (Form-D). Unconditional Oxford offer for the year. Meets Oxford's English requirement. Must not hold another scholarship
english: Oxford English requirement (IELTS/TOEFL usually; MOI not generally accepted)
deadline: 2026-27 call announced Dec 2025; the closing date is not published in coverage found. The 2027-28 call is likely after Oxford offers (early 2027)
bond: Not stated; government-funded, so a return/service condition is possible (unconfirmed)
fitReason: This is the main Sindh-only overseas award, and the applicant has Karachi domicile. It needs an Oxford offer (Oxford deadlines are Dec 2026/Jan 2027) and English test scores. The GPA makes admission a stretch.
steps: Apply to an Oxford MSc (e.g. Advanced Computer Science) by its December 2026/January 2027 deadline
Watch oxpakprogramme.org and the Sindh College Education Department for the 2027-28 call
Apply online on the Oxford Pakistan Programme site with your Sindh domicile, PRC and Oxford offer
Interview if shortlisted

name: Sindh Educational Endowment Fund (SEEF) Scholarship
host: Sindh Educational Endowment Fund Trust, Government of Sindh
coverage: Tuition and allowances at partner Sindh/Pakistani universities
level: Bachelor's/professional mainly; MS(CS) included in some years
eligibility: Sindh domicile + PRC, low-income/merit, full-time at a partner institution in Pakistan
deadline: 2024 cycle closed 30 Sep 2024; annual calls are around Aug-Sep
fitReason: Domestic only: no overseas study component was found. Of no use for studying abroad.
steps: No action for abroad

name: HEC Overseas Scholarship (MS/MPhil leading to PhD) Phase-III
coverage: Tuition (up to the project cap), monthly stipend, health insurance, airfare
amount: Per HEC financial provisions; up to 24 months for MS
fields: Thematic areas incl. 'Digital Transformation & Emerging Technologies' (CS/AI fits)
eligibility: Pakistani/AJK national, 16 years of education, CGPA >= 3.0, age <= 30 (non-employees) on the closing date, HAT test. Universities ranked in the QS/THE top 200
english: No HEC minimum; the host university may require IELTS/TOEFL
gre: Not required by HEC (HAT required); may be required by the host university
deadline: Batch-IV closed 28 Aug 2026 (HAT 19/27 Sep 2026). Batch-V for Fall 2027 is not announced; expect a similar mid-2027 window
bond: YES: a Deed of Agreement & Surety Bond plus a service undertaking. HEC normally requires returning and serving in Pakistan (usually 5 years) or refunding the full cost with a penalty. Confirm the terms in the bond template
fitReason: Large award and CS/AI fits, but the return-and-serve bond conflicts with the plan to earn abroad. Top-200 German universities (TUM, KIT, RWTH, TU Berlin) qualify, so it could fund a German master's.
steps: Watch hec.gov.pk for the Phase-III Batch-V advert (likely Jun-Aug 2027)
Register on the HEC e-Portal and pay the Rs 3,000 fee via 1LINK
Take the HAT (ETC); the score is valid for 2 years
Get unconditional admission to a QS/THE top-200 university (this may waive the test and interview)
Read the Surety Bond / service undertaking before accepting

name: Stipendium Hungaricum (Pak-Hungary, via HEC nomination)
host: Tempus Public Foundation (Hungary) with HEC as nominating body
coverage: Tuition waiver, monthly stipend (about HUF 43,700), dormitory or housing contribution, medical insurance
fields: Many English programmes in CS / data science / AI (ELTE, BME, Debrecen, Szeged)
eligibility: Pakistani national; apply on both the HEC and SH portals; HEC written test >= 50%; Hungarian university test/interview
english: Per university; many Hungarian universities accept an MOI letter or their own online test
deadline: 2026-27 deadline was 15 Jan 2026; the 2027-28 deadline is expected about 15 Jan 2027 (dual portal)
bond: None found from Hungary; HEC may require an undertaking to return (check)
fitReason: Fully funded EU master's in CS/AI in English, often without IELTS. The deadline lines up with a Fall 2027 start. It could replace Germany or serve as a backup.
steps: Open the HEC Stipendium Hungaricum page in Nov-Dec 2026 for the 2027-28 call
Apply on stipendiumhungaricum.hu (choose 2 programmes) AND on the HEC portal by ~15 Jan 2027
Take the HEC written test, then the Hungarian university interview
Results come about May-June 2027

name: Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC Type-A, via HEC)
coverage: Tuition, accommodation, monthly stipend (CNY 3,000 for master's), insurance
fields: CS/AI programmes taught in English at many universities
eligibility: Pakistani national; HEC nomination; university pre-acceptance strongly encouraged
deadline: 2026-27 HEC deadline was 5 Jan 2026 (25 master's seats); expect ~early Jan 2027
fitReason: Fully funded with no IELTS needed, but post-study work in China is very limited, which undercuts the 'earn abroad' goal.
steps: Watch the HEC CGSP page in Nov-Dec 2026
Apply on the CSC portal plus the HEC portal; attach a pre-admission letter

name: HEC-USAID Merit and Needs-Based Scholarship
coverage: Tuition and stipend at Pakistani partner universities
eligibility: Domestic study only; recent rounds were for female students only
deadline: No current round found (USAID funding largely wound down in 2025)
fitReason: Domestic only and female-only in recent rounds, so it cannot fund study abroad.
steps: No action

name: Punjab Educational Endowment Fund (PEEF)
coverage: Tuition/stipend at Punjab partner institutions
eligibility: Punjab domicile ONLY; parental income <= Rs 60,000/month; partner institutions in Pakistan
deadline: Annual (2025-26 cycle)
fitReason: Not eligible: Punjab domicile only, while the applicant is from Sindh. It is also domestic only.
steps: No action

name: Ihsan Trust Qarz-e-Hasna (interest-free education loan)
coverage: Tuition at 130+ partner universities in Pakistan, paid directly to the university
amount: Interest-free; token repayment starts during studies
eligibility: Pakistani; need-cum-merit; CGPA >= 2.5; student of a partner university
deadline: Last call closed 15 Jan 2026 (via partner universities / portal.ihsantrust.org)
fitReason: No study-abroad product found; it is tied to partner universities in Pakistan.
steps: Optionally email Ihsan Trust to ask whether any foreign-study case is ever considered

name: Pakistani bank education loans for study abroad (Bank Alfalah, NBP, Meezan)
host: Bank Alfalah / National Bank of Pakistan / Meezan Bank
coverage: Bank Alfalah has advertised loans for tuition, living and application fees abroad, disbursed in foreign currency yearly. NBP's Students Loan Scheme is domestic. No Meezan study-abroad product was found
amount: Varies; market-rate (KIBOR+) interest, collateral or guarantor needed
eligibility: Pakistani; admission letter; guarantor/collateral; parental income documents
deadline: Rolling
fitReason: This could finance part of the €11.9k German blocked account, but high Pakistani interest rates make it costly. The details are from a 2020 guide; confirm current terms at a branch.
steps: Visit Bank Alfalah (and HBL/UBL) branches in Karachi with an admission letter and ask about the study-abroad loan
Compare the rate against a family loan; check whether funds can be sent to a German blocked account (Fintiba/Expatrio)

name: Akhuwat Qarz-e-Hasna education loan / Karandaaz
coverage: Akhuwat: interest-free tuition loans for low-income students at Pakistani universities. Karandaaz: SME/digital finance investor, no student loan found
amount: Small (e.g. up to Rs 75,000 in the IBA partnership)
eligibility: Low-income, admission in Pakistan
deadline: Rolling
fitReason: Domestic only, and the amounts are far too small. Beware of the many fake 'Akhuwat loan' .it.com sites.
steps: No action; use only akhuwat.org.pk if checking

name: Prime Minister / federal government overseas scholarship schemes
coverage: Past PM scheme (2022-23): 35 MS + 40 PhD awards at QS/THE top-25 universities
eligibility: Unconditional admission to a top-25 university
deadline: Last round closed March 2023; no current round found
fitReason: Not currently running, and it needs top-25 admission. Watch HEC in case it is relaunched.
steps: Monitor hec.gov.pk scholarship announcements

name: Commonwealth Shared Scholarships (UK)
coverage: Tuition, living stipend, airfare, visa
fields: Programmes chosen by participating UK universities, linked to development themes (some include data science/AI)
eligibility: Citizen and permanent resident of an eligible Commonwealth country (Pakistan IS on the list). Not studied/worked more than 1 year in a high-income country. Must be unable to afford UK study
english: University requirement; some UK universities accept MOI from Pakistan
deadline: 2026 round closed 9 Dec 2025. The 2027 round is expected to close ~Dec 2026 (each university sets its own deadline)
bond: Expected to return home after the award (CSC policy; Graduate visa use is restricted)
fitReason: Pakistan is eligible and some UK universities accept MOI. But the return expectation conflicts with the plan to earn abroad, and courses must be development-relevant.
steps: Check cscuk.fcdo.gov.uk in Oct-Nov 2026 for participating universities and courses
Apply to the course, then to the university's Shared Scholarship by its Dec 2026 deadline

name: Chevening Scholarship (2028/29 cycle)
coverage: Tuition, living stipend, flights, visa
eligibility: 2,800 hours of post-degree work. 3 UK course applications plus an unconditional offer by July. Must return to Pakistan for 2 years after the award
english: English requirement now handled through university offers; MOI accepted where the university accepts it
deadline: 2027/28 window was 4/5 Aug-6 Oct 2026 (closed). 2028/29 is expected Aug-early Oct 2027 for a Sept 2028 start
bond: YES: must return to home country for at least 2 years after the scholarship
fitReason: The work-hours rule fits, but the 2-year return rule and a 2028 start conflict with the earn-abroad plan and the 2027 timeline.
steps: Optional fallback: apply Aug-Oct 2027 at chevening.org/apply for 2028 entry

name: Fulbright Degree Program, Pakistan (USEFP), 2028 cohort
coverage: Full tuition, stipend, travel, insurance
eligibility: Pakistani; 16 years of education; GRE General required (min ~145 per section); TOEFL for shortlisted candidates
english: TOEFL required for shortlisted candidates (MOI not accepted)
deadline: 2027 program deadline was about 1 April 2026; the 2028 program is expected about Apr 2027 for a Fall 2028 start
bond: YES: J-1 two-year home-country physical presence requirement (212(e)), so you must return to Pakistan for 2 years before most US/H-1B routes
fitReason: Needs the GRE and TOEFL, starts in 2028 not 2027, and the J-1 2-year home rule blocks working abroad after graduation.
steps: Only if plans change: take the GRE by Mar 2027 and apply on usefp.org

name: Knight-Hennessy (Stanford), Schwarzman (Tsinghua), Yenching Academy (Peking)
coverage: Full funding
fields: KH: any Stanford grad programme (MS CS needs GRE/TOEFL). Schwarzman: Global Affairs master's. Yenching: China Studies master's
eligibility: KH: bachelor's within the last 7 years. Schwarzman: age 18-28, leadership. Yenching: under 30
english: TOEFL/IELTS typically required; MOI not accepted for Stanford
gre: Required for Stanford MS CS; not for Schwarzman/Yenching
deadline: KH ~early Oct; Schwarzman ~mid-Sept; Yenching ~early Dec (all for the following autumn, 2027 entry)
fitReason: KH is closed for 2027 and needs the GRE/TOEFL. Schwarzman and Yenching are not CS/AI degrees and give no work rights for earning abroad.
steps: Skip

name: Google / Microsoft / Meta / NVIDIA graduate fellowships; Women Techmakers
coverage: Tuition + stipend
eligibility: Enrolled PhD students nominated by their university. Women Techmakers scholarship is for women and has largely been discontinued
deadline: Varies (PhD cycles)
fitReason: Not eligible: PhD-only. Women Techmakers is for women.
steps: Revisit only if a PhD follows the master's

name: Not eligible: AAUW International Fellowships, Mastercard Foundation Scholars, Zakat Foundation, Erasmus+ ICM
host: AAUW / Mastercard Foundation / Zakat Foundation of America / EU Erasmus+
coverage: Various
eligibility: AAUW: women only. Mastercard Foundation: African nationals only. Zakat Foundation of America scholarships: US-based students. Erasmus+ International Credit Mobility: short exchange for students currently enrolled at a partner institution such as FAST, so not available after graduating
deadline: N/A
fitReason: Not eligible: male, Pakistani, already graduated. Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (a different Erasmus+ action) IS open to Pakistanis and is worth checking separately.
steps: Skip; look at Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (EMJM) catalogue instead
